# Drop the unused `inspect-ai` dependency and the `[eval]` extra it is the sole content of

## Context / Problem

Per the OPERATOR DECISION comment on this ticket (2026-08-07): **Option A — drop inspect-ai.**
The original scope (smoke-test the inspect-ai eval path) is void because there is no such path.

`inspect-ai>=0.3.221` is declared at `pyproject.toml:150` as the only member of the `[eval]`
extra, and rebar never imports it: `grep -rn "inspect_ai" src/` returns exactly one hit,
`src/rebar/_optional.py:36`, which is the extras-registry NAME string, not an import. There are
zero `import inspect_ai` / `from inspect_ai` statements. `INSPECT_MIN_VERSION` at
`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:40` is referenced by nothing else in the tree.

Carrying it costs three separate pieces of live machinery, all of which exist only for it:

1. Both `[tool.uv] conflicts` entries (`pyproject.toml:275-278`, `eval` vs `bedrock` and `eval`
   vs `dev`) — `[eval]` -> inspect-ai -> aioboto3 -> aiobotocore pins `boto3 < 1.40.62` against
   `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]` needing `boto3 >= 1.42.63`.
2. `override-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]` (`pyproject.toml:285-287`) — inspect-ai caps
   `click < 8.2.2`, which held the whole universal lock on click 8.2.1 and made CI's gating
   pip-audit fail on every in-flight change (PYSEC-2026-2132).
3. This ticket's own premise: a pytest smoke test gated on `[eval]` would run in zero lanes,
   because the eval/dev conflict keeps pytest and inspect-ai out of the same environment.

## Approach

Delete the dependency and everything that exists solely to accommodate it, then let the
resolver prove the accommodations were unnecessary rather than asserting it.

The `[eval]` extra is **removed entirely**, not retained empty. inspect-ai is its only member,
so once removed the extra installs nothing. It is not redefined as an alias for `[agents]`
either: the offline prompt-eval surface (`rebar prompt eval`, spec validation, grader
discipline, JUnit conversion) is stdlib-only and needs no extra, and the live run's own solver
already documents its real requirement as the `agents` extra
(`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`, `_live_solver`: "Needs the `agents` extra (pydantic_ai)").
An alias extra would make `extra_installed("eval")` a synonym for `extra_installed("agents")`
— a second name for one capability, which is the machinery this change is deleting.

Each removal is checked against the resolver before it is kept: `uv lock` is regenerated and
`uv sync --locked` is run for the extra combinations the conflicts previously forked apart.
Both conflicts entries name the `eval` extra, so deleting the extra necessarily deletes them —
a conflict cannot reference an extra that does not exist. The acceptance criterion that no
conflicts entry names `eval` therefore governs absolutely. Should the resolver nonetheless
fail without one of them, that is a blocking discovery about a dependency diamond unrelated to
inspect-ai: it is recorded on this ticket and escalated, not worked around by keeping a
dangling conflict — there is no partial-land path for that branch.

Back-out is a straight `git revert` of the `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` changes, which
restores the extra and its accommodations exactly. No deprecation window is offered: `[eval]`'s
sole member is never imported, so the extra delivered no functional capability to any consumer
and there is nothing for a deprecation period to keep working. `pip` treats an unknown extra as
a warning rather than an error, so an existing `nava-rebar[eval]` pin keeps installing the base
package instead of failing; `uv sync --extra eval` does fail, and the release notes say so.

Removing a published extra is a deliberate consumer-visible break, so it is documented in both
`CHANGELOG.md` (user-facing) and `docs/release-notes.md` (agent-visible contract changes), per
the split those two files declare in their own headers.

The stale docstring is fixed in the same change because it is the same falsehood. That
docstring makes the claim **twice** — line 6 ("runs through **Inspect AI**") and line 21 ("only
the actual *run* (`run_eval`) imports Inspect AI, lazily, behind `guard_import`") — and both are
contradicted by the same file: the comment above the live-run section says "NOT routed through
Inspect AI ... would add a dependency and an impedance mismatch for no gain", and `_live_solver`
imports `rebar.llm.config` / the pydantic-ai runtime, never `inspect_ai`. Both claims are
rewritten to describe the native solver loop that actually runs.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — remove the `eval` extra and its comment block; remove both `[tool.uv]
  conflicts` entries; remove `override-dependencies`; update the `botocore`/`boto3` floor
  comment in `[dev]` that explains itself by reference to the conflicts fork; update the
  lean-install comment at line 59 that names `inspect_ai`.
- `uv.lock` — regenerated with `uv lock`.
- `src/rebar/_optional.py` — drop the `"eval"` entry from `EXTRAS` and the `[eval]` bullet
  from the module docstring.
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py` — rewrite the module docstring to describe the native
  solver loop it actually runs; delete `INSPECT_MIN_VERSION`.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — drop `"eval_extra"` from `available_backends()`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py` — four live references to the extra: drop `eval` from
  the extras probed (line 239) and printed (line 283) by `rebar llm setup`, and correct the two
  places that misstate the live prompt-eval requirement as the `eval` extra — the `_prompt_eval`
  docstring (line 22) and the hint it prints (line 93). Both become `agents`, which is what
  `_live_solver` actually needs.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/*.eval.yaml` and `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/README.plan-review.md` —
  the header comments that tell a reader a live run needs the `[eval]` extra; same correction to
  `[agents]`.
- `README.md` — the `[eval]` bullet under optional capabilities (line 179), the
  `pip install 'nava-rebar[eval]'` recipe (line 227), **and** the union recipe on line 229,
  `pip install 'nava-rebar[agents,eval,tracing]'`, which names the extra in combined form and
  would otherwise stay in the README as a documented command naming a removed extra.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — the `[eval]` extra bullet and the two `[bedrock]`-conflicts-with-
  `[eval]` statements.
- `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md:171` — the prose lists `inspect_ai` as a member of the
  lean-install ban-list this change edits. The ADR's *decision* is untouched; only that
  sentence's claim about live CI machinery is corrected, so the ADR does not describe a
  ban-list entry that no longer exists.
- `docs/dependency-advisory-runbook.md` — its worked `override-dependencies` example IS this
  inspect-ai/PYSEC-2026-2132 override, with a `REMOVE-WHEN` note this change moots. The example
  and every phrase `tests/unit/test_dependency_advisory_wiring.py` pins stay (they are the
  banked uv knowledge); a short note records that this particular override was retired by
  deleting the capping dependency rather than by waiting for upstream — the cheaper remedy the
  runbook should teach first.
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` — every mention of the extra, not only the install: the
  `eval-live` job's `uv sync --locked --extra agents --extra eval` (line 72) and the conflict
  comment above it (line 69), the step name on line 68, the workflow-header comment on line 11
  ("needs the `[agents,eval]` extras + credentials"), and the job's display `name:` on line 52.
  After the change the job installs `--extra agents` only, and nothing in the file advertises a
  removed extra.
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — remove `inspect_ai` from the lean-install
  must-not-import probe list.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release-notes.md` — the breaking-change entries.
- `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py`, `tests/unit/grounding/test_non_adoption.py` — remove
  `inspect_ai` from their must-not-be-imported module lists.
- `tests/unit/test_new_eval_specs.py`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py` — their module docstrings each tell a reader the live
  eval run "needs the `[eval]` extra + credentials", which is the same misstatement being
  corrected in the CLI hints and the spec headers; retarget all three to `agents`.
- `tests/unit/test_optional.py`, `tests/unit/test_llm_setup_cli.py` — retarget the assertions
  that name the `eval` extra onto **`tracing`**, chosen because it is the other net-new extra
  those tests already reference and, like `eval` was, it is absent from the dev venv — so
  `test_require_extra_missing_raises_with_install_hint` keeps exercising the missing-extra
  branch instead of skipping.
- `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py` (new) — the contract tests below.

## Testing

New tests in `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py`, parsing `pyproject.toml` with
`tomllib` (stdlib, Python >= 3.11 per the project's own floor):

- happy path: `inspect-ai` appears in no dependency list anywhere in `pyproject.toml`, and no
  `eval` key exists in `[project.optional-dependencies]`.
- the two accommodations are gone and stay gone: `[tool.uv]` has no `override-dependencies`
  key, and no `conflicts` entry mentions the `eval` extra.
- edge/regression: every extra name in `rebar._optional.EXTRAS` resolves to a real key in
  `[project.optional-dependencies]` — so a future extras rename cannot leave the registry
  pointing at an extra that does not exist (the exact drift this change is fixing by hand).

Resolver + audit evidence, run in the worktree and recorded on the ticket:

- `uv lock` regenerates cleanly, and `uv sync --locked --extra dev`,
  `--extra dev --extra bedrock`, and `--extra dev --extra agents` all resolve and install —
  the dev+bedrock combination is the one the removed conflicts previously forked.
- `pip-audit` over the resulting `dev` environment passes with no `override-dependencies`
  present, confirming the override was a workaround for inspect-ai's stale click cap and not
  load-bearing on its own.
- the full gate — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the pytest suite — passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `grep -rn "inspect.ai\|inspect_ai" pyproject.toml src/ tests/ .github/` returns no
      dependency, import, registry, or probe hit (docs/CHANGELOG history may still mention it).
- [x] `[project.optional-dependencies]` has no `eval` key, verified by the new tomllib test.
- [x] `[tool.uv]` has no `override-dependencies` key and no `conflicts` entry naming `eval`,
      verified by the new tomllib test.
- [x] `uv lock` regenerates `uv.lock` and `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra bedrock`
      installs successfully — the combination the removed conflicts previously forbade.
- [x] `pip-audit` reports no vulnerability on the locked `dev` environment with the click
      override removed; the installed click is >= 8.3.3.
- [x] `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py` has no `INSPECT_MIN_VERSION` and neither docstring claim
      (line 6 and line 21) survives, so the module header no longer contradicts the
      implementation comment above its live-run section.
- [x] `grep -rn "eval\] extra\|nava-rebar\[eval\]" src/ tests/ README.md docs/llm-framework.md`
      returns nothing: no remaining text in code, tests, or user documentation tells a reader
      that a live run needs the removed extra, and no documented install command names it —
      including README.md's `[agents,eval,tracing]` union recipe. The surviving hints name
      `agents`.
- [x] `grep -rn "eval_extra" src/rebar/` returns nothing, so `available_backends()` no longer
      reports a key for the removed extra.
- [x] `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` and `docs/dependency-advisory-runbook.md` no
      longer describe `inspect_ai` as a current lean-install ban-list entry or the click
      override as an active workaround: the ADR's ban-list sentence drops `inspect_ai`, and the
      runbook records that this override was retired by deleting the capping dependency (while
      keeping every phrase `tests/unit/test_dependency_advisory_wiring.py` pins, which still
      pass).
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased) and `docs/release-notes.md` each carry an entry stating that
      the `[eval]` extra is removed and what a consumer installing it should do instead.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full pytest suite pass.
